subject: Model comparison using a multilevel structure via Stan

messages.author: ff9e47f6a1af1908
messages.subject: Model comparison using a multilevel structure via Stan
parts:
I have a latent variable model and I also have the version of the same model using a multilevel structure. I want to compare the fit of both models. At first I thought of using the DIC, WAIC and LOO measures, but I'm realizing that it will not be easy because of this integral in the likelihood function. So I'm researching new ways to compare models. There are authors who defend the use of marginal log density (LMD) to compare hierarchical models, but I need help. Professor Bob Carpenter suggested that I calculate y-predicted from the posterior predictive p(y-predicted | y) and use those to evaluate event probabilities such as Pr[y_predict in (a, b) | y]. But I don't know how to do this via Stan. I would also like to know some theoretical references on the subject.

Thanks,
Marcelo da Silva

messages.subject: Re: Model comparison using a multilevel structure via Stan
parts:
I'm sorry for the delay, Professor Vehtari. I am sending the Stan code of the model in question. What is happening in this code is that I think the way to calculate the likelihood function is wrong, because, from what I've studied, it is necessary to marginalize the likelihood of the betas parameters. I imagine if it were possible to do this in the Stan code, that would be enough, because the R code I think is correct.

I need a lot to calculate at least one of the five measures (DIC, EAIC, EBIC, WAIC or LOO) to compare the fit of this model with the version of the model without considering the multilevel structure.

I commented the code so everyone could understand. Let me know if you need anything else.

Stan code:

data {
  int<lower=1> N;                //total individual
  int<lower=1> J;                //total items
  int<lower=1> m;                //number of categories
  int<lower=1> g;                //number of groups
  int<lower=1> n[g];             //vector of number individual by group
  int<lower=1> gg[N];            //vector index of group
  int<lower=0, upper=m> Y[N, J]; //response matrix
  int<lower=0> X[N, 2];          //covariates matrix
  cov_matrix[3] Sigma;           //covariance matrix
}

transformed data {
  int<lower=1> maxN;
  maxN <- max(n);
}

parameters {
  real<lower=0> a[J];  //discrimination
  real b_aux[J, m-1];  //item difficulty
  vector[3] gamma;     //fixed effects
  vector[3] beta[g];   //random effects
  vector[N] theta;     //latent variables
  real<lower=0> sigma_theta;
}

transformed parameters {
  simplex[m] prob[N, J];
  real eta[N, J, m];
  vector[m] psum[N, J];
  real b[J, m];
  for (j in 1:J) {
    b[j, 1] <- 0;
    for (k in 2:m)
      b[j, k] <- b_aux[j, k-1];
  }
  for (i in 1:N) {
    for (j in 1:J) {
      for (k in 1:m) {
eta[i, j, k] <- a[j] * (theta[i] - b[j, k]);
        psum[i, j, k] <- sum(eta[i, j, 1:k]);
      }
    }
  }
  for (i in 1:N) {
    for (j in 1:J) {
      prob[i, j, 1:m] <- softmax(psum[i, j, 1:m]);
    }
  }
}

model {
  sigma_theta ~ inv_gamma(1, 0.1);
  gamma[1] ~ normal(0, 1);
  gamma[2] ~ normal(0, 1);
  gamma[3] ~ normal(0, 1);
  for (h in 1:g) {
    beta[h] ~ multi_normal(gamma, Sigma);
  }
  for (i in 1:N) {
    theta[i] ~ normal(beta[gg[i], 3] + beta[gg[i], 1] * X[i, 1] + beta[gg[i], 2] * X[i, 2], sigma_theta);
  }
  for (j in 1:J) {
    a[j] ~ normal(1, 2.5) T[0,];
    b_aux[j] ~ normal(0, 2.5);
  }
  for (i in 1:N) {
    for (j in 1:J) {
      Y[i, j] ~ categorical(prob[i, j, 1:m]);
    }
  }
}

generated quantities {
  real dev; //deviance
  vector[J] log_lik[N];
  dev <- 0;
  for (i in 1:N) {
    for (j in 1:J) {
      log_lik[i, j] <- categorical_log(Y[i, j], prob[i, j, 1:m]);
      dev <- dev + (-2) * log_lik[i, j];
    }
  }
}

messages.author: a236d3d356ca53fd
messages.subject: Re: Model comparison using a multilevel structure via Stan
parts:
Hi,

No problem with the delay, I'm not in a hurry :)

I must admit that I'm not deeply familiar with IRT models, so it is possible that I'm missing something specific to them, but as I read the code it seems sensible and especially the way you compute log_lik is correct compare to the model for Y. Stan is sampling from the posterior of betas, too, and log_lik's are derived quantities of beta's. Stan returns draws from the posterior of log_lik and the loo package can use these to compute the loo posterior predictive densities which then includes the integration over all parameters including beta's (see longer explanation in Aki Vehtari, Andrew Gelman and Jonah Gabry (2016). Practical Bayesian model evaluation using leave-one-out cross-validation and WAIC. In Statistics and Computing, doi:10.1007/s11222-016-9696-4 https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.04544). I recommend using loo values given by the loo package, but if you have to use WAIC, they are also based on the loo posterior predictive densities and thus include integration over beta. 

Aki

messages.author: ff9e47f6a1af1908
messages.subject: Re: Model comparison using a multilevel structure via Stan
parts:
Hello dear professor,

Let me know if I understood:
(1) From what I've studied, I concluded that multilevel models need to have verisimilitude marginalized by random effects, such as the figure I've shown, by Fox (2010).
(2) Despite the fact in (1), the likelihood in my Stan code is correct (although I do not consider integration over betas).
(3) Integration over betas can be considered approximately by later predictive densities.

So, from this code in the R, the WAIC and loo measurements would be being calculated from the posteriori predictive density and, therefore, considering the integration of betas, how do I want it?

library(rstan)
library(loo)

waic <- function(stanfit){
  log_lik <- extract (stanfit, "log_lik")$log_lik
  dim(log_lik) <- if (length(dim(log_lik))==1) c(length(log_lik),1) else
  c(dim(log_lik)[1], prod(dim(log_lik)[2:length(dim(log_lik))]))
  S <- nrow(log_lik)
  n <- ncol(log_lik)
  lpd <- log(colMeans(exp(log_lik)))
  p_waic <- colVars(log_lik)
  elpd_waic <- lpd - p_waic
  waic <- -2*elpd_waic
  loo_weights_raw <- 1/exp(log_lik-max(log_lik))
  loo_weights_normalized <- loo_weights_raw/
  matrix(colMeans(loo_weights_raw),nrow=S,ncol=n,byrow=TRUE)
  loo_weights_regularized <- pmin (loo_weights_normalized, sqrt(S))
  elpd_loo <- log(colMeans(exp(log_lik)*loo_weights_regularized)/
  colMeans(loo_weights_regularized))
  p_loo <- lpd - elpd_loo
  pointwise <- cbind(waic,lpd,p_waic,elpd_waic,p_loo,elpd_loo)
  total <- colSums(pointwise)
  se <- sqrt(n*colVars(pointwise))
  return(list(waic=total["waic"], elpd_waic=total["elpd_waic"],
  p_waic=total["p_waic"], elpd_loo=total["elpd_loo"], p_loo=total["p_loo"],
  pointwise=pointwise, total=total, se=se))
}
...
stanfit <- stan(...)
calc.WAIC <- waic(stanfit)
calc.LOO  <- loo(extract_log_lik(stanfit))

messages.author: a236d3d356ca53fd
messages.subject: Re: Model comparison using a multilevel structure via Stan
parts:
Hi,

Stan is sampling from the joint posterior distribution including betas. Using the obtained draws you can approximate the integration over betas. I recommend to read some introduction to Monte Carlo (and Markov chain Monte Carlo) methods to understand how Monte Carlo integration works.

Instead of using truncated importance sampling and WAIC as in the code you posted, we recommend using PSIS-LOO. If you are 100% certain that you need WAIC, you can get that using loo package, too.

Aki
